channel.title: Vito Lin
channel.description: Vito Lin writes Rust close to the metal and CUDA close to the silicon, and sends the fixes upstream.

item.title: Pretraining and fine-tuning nanoGPT-124M from scratch
item.description: Building a 124M-parameter GPT-2 from scratch, then turning it from a text-completion model into an instruction-following one with SFT — plus the systems bugs that ate more time than the model itself.

item.title: Paper notes: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
item.description: GQA and document masking in Llama 3's architecture, and the 4D parallelism strategy — TP, CP, PP, DP — that Meta used to fit the 405B run across a topology-aware cluster.

item.title: Paper notes: PagedAttention
item.description: PagedAttention as virtual memory, copy-on-write prefix sharing, and all-or-nothing preemption — reading the vLLM paper as a catalogue of OS techniques applied to the KV cache.

item.title: Paper notes: Trading More Storage for Less Computation
item.description: Notes on Mooncake's FAST '25 paper: disaggregated prefill/decode, a cluster-wide KVCache pool, and prefix hashing that skips prefill on a cache hit.

item.title: Resources that helped me transition into AI Infrastructure
item.description: Everything I read, watched, and cloned this year while moving into AI Infrastructure — GPU programming, LLM internals, and the systems around serving them.

item.title: Register tiling: the foundation of high-performance CUDA GEMM
item.description: Shared memory isn't the end of the optimization pipeline — how loading tile fragments into registers gets 2.5x–3x more throughput than shared memory alone, and why register pressure is the tradeoff that limits it.

item.title: Becoming a contributor to NVIDIA's cuda-oxide
item.description: cuda-oxide compiles Rust directly to PTX, with no wrappers, DSLs, or FFI overhead. Notes on why that excites me, and on the patches I contributed to get there.

item.title: How CUDA is executed by the GPU
item.description: Between a .cu file and Tensor Cores sits a multi-stage compiler pipeline — CUDA C++, PTX, ptxas, SASS, and the fatbins that let one binary run on both an RTX 3090 and an H100.

item.title: Why adding just 1 block can drop GPU utilization to 67%
item.description: Wave quantization: why grid sizes that don't divide evenly across SMs leave a nearly-idle last wave, why persistent kernels only half-fix it, and how Stream-K splits the remainder across SMs instead.

item.title: What GPU hardware really taught me
item.description: SMs, warps, and SIMT execution — why GPU performance is about latency hiding and occupancy rather than raw thread count, and why memory, not compute, is usually the real bottleneck.

item.title: How to practice CUDA without a GPU (for free)
item.description: You don't need to own an NVIDIA GPU to start learning CUDA — a rundown of eight cloud platforms with free GPU access, from Colab and Kaggle to CUDA-specific practice sites.

item.title: CUDA matrix multiplication: optimizing with shared memory and tiling
item.description: The difference between a slow and a fast matmul kernel isn't thread count — it's memory access pattern. How tiling turns a memory-bound problem into a compute-efficient one.

item.title: CUDA's memory model: why memory, not compute, is the bottleneck
item.description: Registers, shared memory, global memory, constant memory, texture memory — where each one sits on-chip or off-chip, and why most CUDA performance issues trace back to global memory.

item.title: CUDA's execution model: threads, warps, and how the GPU schedules them
item.description: The thread/block/grid hierarchy, why GPUs schedule warps instead of individual threads, and why launch configuration is a performance decision, not just boilerplate.

item.title: First CUDA program: vector addition
item.description: The host/device split and the six-step memory dance every CUDA program follows — allocate, copy to GPU, execute, copy back, free — starting from the simplest possible kernel.
